id: A Biholomorphism of the Unit Disk with f(0)=0 is Linear
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $f:\D\rightarrow \D$ be a biholomorphism such that $f(0)=0$. Show that
$$
f(z) = cz
$$
for some $\abs{c}=1$.

id: A Complex Trigonometric Inequality
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Determine all points $z\in \C$ such that
$$
\abs{\cos(z)}^2 + \abs{\sin(z)}^2 \leq 1.
$$

id: A Condition for the Existence of a Holomorphic Logarithm on the Punctured Plane
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $f$ be a holomorphic function on $\Omega = \C\backslash \{0\}$ and assume that
$$
\int_{\abs{z}=1} \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\, dz =0.
$$
Show that $f(z)$ has a holomorphic logarithm on $\Omega$.

id: A Linear Lower Bound for Entire Functions Diverging at Infinity
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $f(z)$ be an entire function such that $\abs{f(z)} \rightarrow \infty$ as $\abs{z}\rightarrow \infty$. Show that there exists constants $c>0,R>0$ such that $\abs{f(z)}>c\abs{z}$ for all $\abs{z}>R$.

id: A Maximum Modulus Estimate on an Annulus
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State the maximum modulus principle
(b) Let $f$ be analytic on an open neighborhood of the annulus $1\leq \abs{z}\leq 2$. Assume that $\abs{f(z)}\leq 1$ for all $\abs{z}=1$, and $\abs{f(z)}\leq 4$ for all $\abs{z}=2$. Show that $\abs{f(z)} \leq \abs{z}^2$ for all $1\leq \abs{z}\leq 2$.

id: A Maximum Principle for the Real Part of a Holomorphic Function
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a connected domain and let $f:\Omega\rightarrow \C$ be holomorphic. Show that if $\Re(f(z))$ attains a maximum on $\Omega$, then $f(z)$ is constant.

id: A Normal Family from an L2 Boundary Bound
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of functions $f$ that are holomorphic in a neighborhood of the unit disk such that
$$
\int_0^{2\pi} \abs{f(e^{it})}^2\, dt \leq 1.
$$
Prove that $\mathcal{F}$ is a normal family in the unit disk.

id: A Unique Zero of a−z−exp(-z) in the Right Half-Plane
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $a>1$. Show that the equation
$$
a-z-e^{-z}=0
$$
has exactly one solution in the right half plane $\Re(z)>0$.

id: All Biholomorphisms of the Complex Plane are Linear
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State the Casorati-Weirstrass Theorem.
(b) Show that the only bi-holomorphic map from $\C$ to itself is of the form $f(z)=az+b$ with $a\neq 0$.

id: An Entire Function with Bounded Product of Real and Imaginary Parts is Constant
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $f=u+iv$ be an entire function such that $\abs{u}\cdot \abs{v}$ is bounded. Show that $f$ is a constant function.

id: Antiderivatives on the Plane Minus the Unit Interval
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Explain why $\displaystyle \frac{\sin(z^2)}{(z-1)(z+1)}$ has an analytic antiderivative on $\C\backslash [-1, 1]$.

id: Comparing Two Branches of a Square Root Identity
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\sqrt[pr]{w}$ denote the principle branch of $w^\frac{1}{2}$ corresponding to 
$$
-\pi < \arg(w)<\pi.
$$
Let
$$
\Omega_L = \{z\in \C : \Re(z)<0\}\backslash[-1, 0), \quad \Omega_R = \{z\in \C : \Re(z)>0\}\backslash(0, 1].
$$
Define
$$
f(z) := \sqrt[pr]{z-1}\sqrt[pr]{z+1} \quad \text{ and } \quad g(z):= \sqrt[pr]{z^2-1}
$$
wherever the respective expressions are defined. 
(a) Prove that for all $z\in\Omega_R$, $f(z)=g(z)$.
(b) Prove that for all $z\in \Omega_L$, $f(z)=-g(z)$.
(c) What can you say when $z\in i\R$?

id: Comparing z and 1-exp(z) on the disk
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Prove that if $0<\abs{z}<1$, then $\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}\abs{z} < \abs{1-e^z} < \frac{7}{4}\abs{z}$.

id: Conformal Equivalence of a Horizontal Strip and the Unit Disk
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\Omega=\{z\in \C:0<\Im(z)<1\}$.

(a) Find an analytic function $f(z)$ that maps $\Omega$ ont-to-one onto the unit disk. 
(b) show that, for any two points $a_1,a_2 \in \Omega$, there exists a one-to-one conformal map from $\Omega$ onto itself such that $\phi(a_1)=a_2$.

id: Constructing a Conformal Map from a Slit Quadrant to the Unit Disk
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State the Riemann Mapping Theorem
(b) Let 
$$
\Omega = \{z\in \C :\Re(z)>0, \Im(z)>0\}\backslash \{t(1+i):t\in [1,\infty)\}.
$$
Construct an explicit one-to-one conformal map $F:\Omega\rightarrow \D$ such that $F\left(\frac{1+i}{2}\right)=0$ and $F'\left(\frac{1+i}{2}\right)>0$. The answer may be given as a composition of elementary conformal maps.

id: Constructing an Entire Function with a Shift Identity Via an Infinite Product
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let
$$
G(z) = e^{z\gamma} \prod_{k=1}^\infty \left(1+ \frac{z}{k} \right) e^{-\frac{z}{k}}.
$$
(a) Show that this infinite product defines a well-defined entire function.
(b) Prove that
$$
(z+1)G(z+1)=G(z).
$$

id: Constructing the Reciprocal Gamma Function Via an Infinite Product
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let 
$$
G(z) = z\prod_{k=1}^\infty \left(1+ \frac{z}{k} \right) e^{-\frac{z}{k}}.
$$

(a) Show that this infinite product defines a well-defined entire function.
(b) Where are the zeros of this functions? Show your work.
(c) Compute the limit
$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} \frac{z(z+1)(z+2)\cdots(z+n)}{n!} n^{-z}.
$$
   Your answer may be expressed in terms of $G(z)$.

id: Convergence of Derivatives of Sequences of Holomorphic Functions
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\D$ denote the open unit disk in the complex plane and let $f_n$ be a sequence of holomorphic functions that converges uniformly on $\Omega$. Either prove or give counterexamples to the following statements:

(a) $f_n'$ converges uniformly on $\Omega$.
(b) $f_n'$ converges locally uniformly on $\Omega$.

id: Counting Zeros of a Polynomial on an Annulus
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: How many solutions does $3z^7-5z^3+1=0$ have in the annulus $1 < \abs{z}<2$?

id: Counting Zeros of a Polynomial on the Unit Disk
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
How many solutions (up to multiplicity) to the equation
$$
z^7-2z^5+6z^3-z+1=0
$$
lie in the disk $\abs{z}<1$?

id: Counting Zeros of a Truncated Exponential Perturbation
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $m\geq 0$. How many roots does the function
$$
f(z) = 3z+\sum_{n=0}^m \frac{z^n}{n!}
$$
have on the unit disk $\D$? Justify your answer.

id: Counting Zeros of a Truncated Exponential
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
For each $n\in \N$, let
$$
p_n(z) = \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{z^k}{k!}.
$$
Let $Z(n)$ denote the number of zeros of $p_n(z)$ on the open disk of radius $5\pi$ centered at 0. Compute
$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty} Z(n).
$$

id: Counting Zeros of a Truncated Geometric Perturbation
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State Rouche's theorem.
(b) Let 
$$
p_n(z) = z^2 -2 \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{z^k}{3^k}.
$$
Let $Z_n$ denote the number of zeros of $p_n$ (counting multiplicity) on the disk $\{z\in \C:\abs{z-\frac{1}{2}}<1\}$. Determine $\displaystyle \lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}Z_n$.

id: Derivative Bound for Holomorphic Self-Maps Fixing a Point
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Suppose $\Omega$ is a simply connected domain that is not the whole complex plane, and $a$ is a point in $\Omega$. Prove that if $f$ is analytic on $\Omega$ and maps $\Omega$ into $\Omega$ with $f(a)=a$, then $|f'(a)|\leq 1$.

id: Determining All Injective Rational Functions From the Punctured Plane Into Itself
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Determine all rational functions which map $\C\backslash \{0\}$ one-to-one into $\C\backslash \{0\}$.

id: Entire Functions Omitting an Open Disk are Constant
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State Liouville’s Theorem.
(b) Show that if $f(z)$ is an entire function, and there is a nonempty open disk such that $f(z)$ does not attain any values in this disk, then $f(z)$ is constant.

id: Entire Functions of Polynomial Growth are Polynomials
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State Liouville's theorem.
(b) Suppose that $f$ is entire such that there exists $C>0$ and $n\in\N$ such that $\abs{f(z)}\leq C\abs{z}^n$ for all $\abs{z}\geq 1$. Show that $f(z)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $n$.

id: Entire Functions of Sublinear Growth are Constant
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Suppose that $f(z)$ is an entire function such that, for some $C>0$, $\abs{f(z)}\leq C\left(1+\abs{z}\right)^\frac{1}{2}$ for all $z\in \C$. Show that $f(z)$ is constant.

id: Entire Injective Functions are Linear
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Suppose that $f:\C\rightarrow \C$ is entire with $f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n z^n$.

(a) Show that $f$ has an essential singularity at $\infty$ if $a_n\neq 0$ for infinitely many $n\in\N$.
(b) Show that if $f$ is injective, then $f(z) = a_0+a_1z$ with $a_1 \neq 0$.

id: Estimating a Bound for the Set of Roots of a Polynomial Using Rouché's Theorem
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State Rouché's theorem.
(b) Prove that any polynomial with complex coefficients $P(z) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_kz^k$ with $a_n\neq 0$ has exactly $n$ roots, and give an estimate on the radius of the disk centered at 0 $D_R(0)$ containing all roots.

id: Existence of a Holomorphic Cube Root of a Polynomial
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Show that there exists a holomorphic function $g(z)$ on $\Omega:= \C\backslash[0,2]$ such that $g(z)^3 = z(z-1)(z-2)$.

id: Existence of an Antiderivative for 2 Specific Functions
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\Omega := \{z\in \C: \abs{z}>3\}$, and let
$$
f(z)=\frac{z+1}{(z-2)(z^2+3)}, \qquad g(z)=\frac{z^2}{(z-2)(z^2+3)}.
$$
(a) Is there a holomorphic function whose derivative is $f(z)$ on $\Omega$?
(b) Is there a holomorphic function whose derivative is $g(z)$ on $\Omega$?

id: Existence of an Entire Logarithm for Nonzero Entire Functions
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Show that if $f(z)$ is an entire nonzero function, then $f(z)=e^{g(z)}$ for some entire function $g(z)$.

id: Extension of Locally Uniform Convergence Across the Real Axis Given a Bound Off of the Real Line
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $(f_n)$ be a sequence of entire functions converging locally uniformly on $\C\backslash \R$ to a function $f$. Assume, in addition, that
$$
\abs{f_n(z)} \leq \abs{\Im(z)}^{-\frac{1}{2}}
$$
for all $z\in \C\backslash \R$ and all $n\in\N$. Show that $f$ is entire and that $f_n\rightarrow f$ locally uniformly on $\C$.

id: Holomorphic Functions have Isolated Zeros
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $f$ be a holomorphic function on a connected domain $U$. Show that if $f$ is not identically 0, then the zeros of $f$ are isolated.

id: Holomorphic Functions with Controlled Growth on the Punctured Plane
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $s>0$ be a real number. Describe the set of all holomorphic functions $f:\C\backslash \{0\}\rightarrow \C$ for which there exists a constant $A>0$ such that $\abs{f(z)}\leq A \left(1+ \abs{z}^{-s} \right)$ for all $z\in \C\backslash\{0\}$. Prove your statement.

id: Holomorphic Functions with Real Boundary Values
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Suppose $f(z)$ is a complex valued continuous function on the closed unit disc $|z|\leq 1$ that is analytic on the open unit disc $|z|<1$. Suppose further that $f$ maps the unit circle onto the real line. Prove that $f$ must be a real constant function.

id: Holomorphicity Preserves Differentiation Under Uniform Limits
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq \C$ be open and suppose that $(f_n)$ is a sequence of holomorphic functions that converges uniformly to $f:\Omega\rightarrow \C$. Show that, for any $\delta>0$, we have that $f_n'\rightarrow f'$ uniformly on the set
$$
K_\delta := \{z\in \Omega: \overline{B_\delta(z)}\subseteq \Omega \}.
$$

id: Holomorphicity of ℜ(f)*f Implies Constancy
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Suppose $f$ is a holomorphic function on a connected open set, and $u=\Re(f)$. Prove that if the product $u \overline{f}$ is holomorphic, then $f$ must be a constant function.

id: Integrals of Harmonic Functions Are Harmonic
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Suppose that $u:\C\times \R\rightarrow \R$ is continuous such that $u(z,s)$ is harmonic in $z$ for each $s\in \R$. Define
$$
U(z)= \int_{-1}^1 u(z,s)\, ds.
$$
Show that $U$ is harmonic on $\C$.

id: Local Preservation of Zeros Under Uniform Convergence of Holomorphic Functions 1
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) State Rouché's theorem.
(b) Let $(f_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence of holomorphic functions $\Omega\rightarrow \C$ on the open domain $\Omega$, converging uniformly to a limit $f$ on every compact subset of $\Omega$. Show that if $f$ has a zero $z_0$ of order $m$ in $\Omega$, then there exists $r>0$ and $N\in \N$ such that for all $n\geq N$, $f_n$ has exactly $m$ zeros (counted with multiplicity) on the disk $D_r(z_0)$.

id: Local Preservation of Zeros Under Uniform Convergence of Holomorphic Functions 2
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $D\subseteq \C$ be open and connected, let $f_n$ be holomorphic in $D$ for all $n\in \N$, and suppose $f_n\rightarrow f$ uniformly on $D$. Suppose also  there exists $z_0\in D$ such that $f(z_0)=0$, but that $f$ is not identically equal to 0. Prove that there exists $n\in\N$ such that $f_n$ has a zero on $D$.

id: Locally Uniform Limits of Entire Functions are Entire
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Suppose that $(f_n)$ is a sequence of entire functions such that $f_n$ converges locally uniformly to a function $f:\C\rightarrow \C$. Show that $f$ is entire.

id: Maximum Modulus of a Polynomial on the Disk
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: At what point or points in the closed unit disk does $z^6+z^4$ attain its maximum modulus? Explain.

id: Maximum Principle for the Real Parts of Holomorphic Functions
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $R>0$ and let $f$ be holomorphic in the disk $D_R(0) = \{z\in \C : |z|<R\}$. Define $A:[0,R)\rightarrow \R$ by 
$$
A(r)= \sup\{ \Re(f(z)) : |z|=r\}.
$$
Show that if $f$ is non-constant, then $A$ is strictly increasing on $[0,R)$.

id: Possible Values of a Contour Integral
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Suppose that $\gamma$ is a simple, closed, piecewise $C^1$ curve in $\C$. What are all the possible values of
$$
\int_\gamma \frac{z}{z^2+1}\, dz
$$
for different choices of $\gamma$? Explain your reasoning.

id: Proof of Morera's Theorem
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $f$ be a continuous function on a domain $\Omega\subseteq \C$ such that for every closed piecewise $C^1$ curve $\gamma$ in $\Omega$,
$$
\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz =0.
$$
Show that $f$ is holomorphic on $\Omega$.

id: Proof of the Casorati-Weirstrass Theorem
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: State and prove the Casorati-Weirstrass Theorem.

id: Proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: Let $f(z)$ be a nonzero polynomial of degree $n\geq 0$. Show that $f(z)$ has exactly $n$ zeros counted with multiplicity.

id: Proof of the Schwarz Lemma
subject: Complex Analysis
statement: State and Prove the Schwarz lemma.

id: Removing a Piece of the Principle Part of a Function to Obtain an Antiderivative
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $f$ be holomorphic in the punctured unit disk $\D\backslash \{0\}$, let $r\in (0,1)$, and define $\gamma(t):=re^{it}$ for $t\in [0,2\pi]$. Define
$$
c = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_{\gamma} f(z)\, dz,
$$
and let
$$
h(z) := f(z) - \frac{c}{z}.
$$
Prove that $h$ has a holomorphic antiderivative on $\D\backslash\{0\}$.

id: Residue Formula for a Quotient by a Function with a Double Root
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Suppose $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $a$ and that $g$ has a zero of order 2 at $a$. 

(a) Show that $g(z)= (z-a)^2 h(z)$ where $h(z)$ is meromorphic in a punctured neighborhood of $a$ with a removable singularity at $a$. Find the Taylor coefficients for the power series of $h$ centered at $z=a$.
(b) Find the principle part of $\frac{f}{g}$ centered at $z=a$ by computing a small number of coefficients in the Taylor series for $\frac{f}{h}$. Write a formula for the residue of $\frac{f}{g}$ at $z=a$.

id: Residue Theorem Purdue January 2024
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $n \geq 2$. Calculate
$$
\int_0^{\infty} \frac{1}{x^n+1}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory Purdue August 2025
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $a\in (0,1)$. Evaluate 
$$
I(a) = \int_0^{\infty} \frac{x^{-a}}{1+x}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory Purdue January 2025
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $\gamma$ be an elipse where one of the foci is the origin oriented clockwise. Compute
$$
\int_\gamma \frac{e^{5z}}{z^7}\, dz.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2017
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Use residue theory to compute
$$
\int_0^{2\pi} \frac{\cos(\theta)}{4+\cos(\theta)}\, d\theta.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2019
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Evaluate the integral
$$
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{\sin(x)}{x}\,dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2020
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Evaluate the integral
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2021
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
For $a>0$, compute the following integral using residue theory:
$$
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{\cos(x)}{x^2+a^2}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2024
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
For $a\in \C$ with $0<\Re(a)<1$, evaluate
$$
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{e^{ax}}{1+e^x}\, dx
$$
by residues. Justify your limiting process carefully.

id: Residue Theory UCSC Fall 2025
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Compute, using residue theory,
$$
\int_0^{2\pi} \frac{\sin(\theta)}{2+\cos(\theta)}\,d\theta.
$$
Simplify your answer as much as possible.

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2013
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Compute
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin^2(x)}{x^2}\, dx
$$
by showing that
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin^2(x)}{x^2}\, dx=\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin(x)}{x}\,dx
$$
and then computing
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin(x)}{x}\,dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2014
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Evaluate, for $a>0$,
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{\ln(x)}{x^2+a^2}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2018
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Show, using residue theory, that for every $a\in\R$,
$$
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{e^{-2\pi i xa}}{\cosh(\pi x)}\, dx=\frac{1}{\cosh(\pi a)}.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2019
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Using residue theory, compute the integrals
$$
I_1 = \int_0^\infty \frac{1-\cos(x)}{x^2}\,dx, \qquad I_2 = \int_0^{2\pi}\frac{1}{2+\cos(x)}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2021
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Use the residue theorem to compute
$$
\int_0^\infty \frac{x^\frac{1}{3}}{1+x^2}\, dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2023
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $a>0, b\in\R$. Compute, using residue theory, the integrals
$$
\int_0^\infty e^{-ax}\cos(bx)\,dx, \qquad \int_0^\infty e^{-ax}\sin(bx)\,dx.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2024
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $a>0$. Compute, using residue theory, the integral
$$
\int_\R \frac{dx}{(x^2+a^2)^2}.
$$
Justify any limiting processes involved.

id: Residue Theory UCSC Spring 2025
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Compute the following integral using residue theory:
$$
\int_\R \frac{dx}{\left(1+x^2 \right)^3}.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Winter 2018
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
(a) Prove using complex integration that for any $\alpha \in \R$,
$$
\int_\R e^{-(x+ia)^2}\, dx = \int_\R e^{-x^2}\, dx.
$$
(b) Let $\sigma >0, \xi \in \R$. Show that 
$$
\int_\R e^{-ix \xi} e^{-\frac{x^2}{2\sigma^2}}\, dx = \sigma \sqrt{2\pi} e^{-\frac{\sigma^2\xi^2}{2}}.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Winter 2020
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
For each $a\in\R$, compute the following integral using residue theory:
$$
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{e^{iax}}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}\, dx
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Winter 2021
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Use residue theory to evaluate
$$
\int_0^\pi \frac{d\theta}{2+\sin(2\theta)}.
$$

id: Residue Theory UCSC Winter 2022
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Prove that
$$
\int_0^{2\pi} e^{\cos(\theta)}\, d\theta = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{1}{\left(n! 2^n \right)^2}.
$$

id: Simple Zeros Are Stable Under Small Holomorphic Perturbations
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Suppose $f$ and $g$ are holomorphic in a region containing the disk $|z|\leq 1$. Suppose that $f$ has a simple zero at $z=0$ and vanishes nowhere else in $|z|\leq 1$. Let
$$
f_\varepsilon(z)=f(z)+\varepsilon g(z).
$$

(a) Show that for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, $f_\varepsilon$ has a unique zero in $|z|\leq 1$.
(b) For all small $\varepsilon>0$, let $z_\varepsilon$ denote that zero from part (a). Show that the mapping $\varepsilon \mapsto z_\varepsilon$ is continuous.

id: Winding behavior of polynomials on the unit circle
subject: Complex Analysis
statement:
Let $p(z)$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ that is nonzero on the unit circle $\T=\{z\in\C:\abs{z}=1\}$. Define
$$
m_0 := \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_\T \frac{p'(z)}{p(z)}\, dz, \qquad m_1 := \frac{1}{2\pi i} \int_\T z\frac{p'(z)}{p(z)}\, dz.
$$
Show that $m_0\in \{0,\cdots, n\}$ and $\abs{m_1}\leq m_0$.
